title: Perf canary thresholds for FP8/INT8 rollout (noise handling + auto rollback)
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Implement perf-canary gating for FP8/INT8 kernel enablement so we can safely roll out kernel-selection changes by model/region/GPU cohort. Scope includes: threshold profiles (TTFT/TPOT/tokens-s/error rate), noise suppression (small sample + baseline drift), and automatic rollback triggers with clear runbook steps.

Why: We saw early TTFT regressions in limited prompt regimes during kernel bring-up and want a reliable automated guardrail before expanding beyond canary regions. Additionally, current canary alerts are too noisy in low-traffic cohorts; need min-sample + aggregation rules to avoid false positives while still catching real regressions.

Key links:
- Confluence runbook (target doc to update/validate): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/perf-canary-rollout-for-new-kernels.json
- Metric definitions reference: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/fp8-int8-perf-metrics-definitions.json
- Dashboarding companion work: ENG-7427 / Grafana PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-377-add-fp8-int8-benchmark-and-rollout-dashboards.json
- Rollout gating implementation (runtime): sources/github/redwood/pr-19896-perf-canary-gate-new-kernels-by-model-and-region.json
- Threshold profiles (perf-canary): sources/github/perf-canary/pr-611-add-ttft-tpot-threshold-profiles-for-quantized-kernels.json

- Runtime perf architect: Noah Patel

- Perf/Evals sign-off: Jonas Weber (for quality caveats on enable-by-default)

Deliverables:
1) Threshold profile spec and defaults for quantized kernels (FP8/INT8) by GPU SKU (H100/A100/L4) and workload class (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy).
2) Noise handling: min-sample requirements, low-traffic suppression, baseline window and drift handling.
3) Auto rollback: clear triggers + implementation behavior (disable flag for cohort + page/notify) and audit trail.
4) Runbook updates + example Slack comms snippets and how to override/ack while investigating.

Non-goals:
- Designing new metrics (use existing TTFT/TPOT/tokens-s/error rate); tag dimensions come from ENG-7425/PR-19934.
- Deciding final kernel heuristics (tracked in ENG-7430 / ADR-019).
acceptance_criteria:
Functional:
- Canary supports per-(model, region, GPU SKU, kernel_mode) cohort gating with independent thresholds (FP8, INT8, baseline).
- Canary evaluates: TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, tokens/s (throughput proxy), error rate, and optional GPU OOM rate when dimension is available.
- Canary auto-disables the new kernel mode for the cohort on threshold breach and writes an event with reason + metrics snapshot.

Noise handling:
- No alert/rollback for cohorts with < N requests in the evaluation window (default N=250; configurable per model tier).
- Uses comparison against a baseline window (default 7 days) with guardrails for baseline drift; supports re-baselining when a new runtime release becomes baseline.
- Supports "warmup" exclusion: ignore first 10 minutes after enabling a cohort (to avoid cache cold-start artifacts).

Rollout safety:
- Rollback triggers are stricter for customer-facing p95 (TTFT/TPOT) than for p50; error rate triggers override latency-only triggers.
- Explicitly prevents flapping: if rollback triggered once in 24h, lock cohort to baseline until manual ack in #eng-sre.

Docs/ops:
- Runbook updated with: how to interpret breaches, common false positive root causes, where to find dashboards, and how to re-enable safely.
- Slack notification includes cohort dimensions and a link to Grafana slice.

Testing:
- Unit/integration tests cover min-sample suppression, warmup exclusion, drift handling, and flapping lock behavior.
- Staging validation: induce synthetic regression to confirm rollback path disables flag and emits event + Slack notification.
implementation_notes:
Threshold profiles (initial defaults; tuned in collaboration with Allison + Noah):
- H100 cohorts:
  - TTFT p95 regression threshold: +6% vs baseline (hard), +3% (warn)
  - TPOT p95 regression threshold: +4% (hard), +2% (warn)
  - tokens/s drop: -4% (hard)
- A100 cohorts:
  - TTFT p95 regression threshold: +8% (hard)
  - TPOT p95 regression threshold: +6% (hard)
  - tokens/s drop: -5% (hard)
- L4 (cost SKU; higher variance):
  - TTFT p95 regression threshold: +10% (hard) with stricter min-sample (N=400) and longer window

Error-rate triggers (all SKUs):
- +0.15% absolute error-rate increase (hard rollback) OR 2x relative increase if baseline error is very low (<0.1%).

Evaluation window:
- Default: 30 min rolling window for latency/throughput + baseline reference (7d).
- Exclude first 10 min after enable and any known incident windows (from SRE incident annotations).

Noise suppression:
- Min-sample N default 250; higher for L4 and low-traffic models.
- Require breach to persist for 2 consecutive evaluation windows OR exceed "hard" threshold by 2x in a single window.

Flapping prevention:
- After rollback, lock cohort for 24h unless manually acknowledged by oncall (documented in runbook).

rollout_plan:
1) Enable in staging for 24h to validate suppression + rollback.
2) Canary in us-east (H100) for top-2 hosted models with FP8 attention flag; monitor for 12h.
3) Expand to us-west + eu-west (H100) and add INT8 matmul cohorts.
4) Add A100 cohorts after 48h stable; L4 only after min-sample and variance are validated.
5) Any rollback locks cohort for 24h; follow runbook for triage and only re-enable with explicit oncall ack.

Comms: rollback notifications to #eng-sre and #eng-runtime; daily summary in #eng-runtime during sprint window.
